root.name: Latvian Gambit Accepted: Foltys Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. Nxe5 Qf6 4. Nc4 fxe4 5. d3

overview: After 3.Nxe5 Qf6 4.Nc4 fxe4 5.d3 White attacks the e4 pawn and Black can hold it with ...d5 or ...exd3, leaving a messy position with open f-file. Black keeps the queen on f6 and develops quickly, while White hopes the extra development and a safe king gives an edge.

white_ideas.idea: Recapture on e4 or d3 and develop with Nc3

black_ideas.idea: Use the open f-file and bishop to c5

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with Black pawn on e4 and White knight on c4

character.notes: Early queen sortie and tactical open lines make for forcing play.

gambit.notes: Material is level at the root: each side has lost one pawn.

sublines_that_differ.name: Foltys-Leonhardt 4.Nc4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. Nxe5 Qf6 4. Nc4
sublines_that_differ.how: Parent position before Black decides about ...fxe4.

character.reason: Early queen move and open play, where one slip loses quickly.

gambit.reason: Material is level at this position, so no pawn is offered.

soundness.reason: The Latvian is dubious as Black's king and queen are exposed.

structure.reason: The e- and f-pawns have been exchanged, leaving open lines.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly choose the Latvian.

plans.reason: Black's queen comes out early and he uses fast development to compensate.
